# claude-loop-runner

> A Node CLI that drives the Claude Code CLI in an unattended loop against a
> plan you keep in a file. Every iteration is a fresh `claude --print` call, so
> the context window never grows across a long run. Long-term memory lives in
> two markdown files inside the target repository, not in the conversation.

Built and used in production by ROI Labs (https://roilabs.com.br). Source is
public at https://github.com/JeanZorzetti/claude-loop-runner. Free, no account
or service of its own — it runs against your existing Claude Code CLI login.

## What problem it solves

A single long Claude Code session accumulates every turn it has ever taken.
Around task ten or twelve of a multi-day plan, the window is full and the run
either degrades or has to be cleared, losing the thread. claude-loop-runner
never lets that happen: each task starts a new non-interactive process that
reads only two small files, so token usage per iteration stays roughly flat no
matter how long the plan is.

## How it works

- `macro_plan.md` — you write it once, by hand: scope, architecture, ordered
  task list. The run reads it every iteration and never rewrites it.
- `current_state.md` — the run rewrites it after every iteration. YAML
  frontmatter carries `status` (`in_progress` | `done` | `blocked`),
  `next_effort` (`low` | `medium` | `high`), and `iteration`. This file is the
  entire handoff between one call and the next.
- Tag a task `[low]`, `[medium]` or `[high]` in the plan and the runner passes
  that to `claude --effort`, so how much deliberation each step gets is decided
  in advance, in writing.
- One iteration: confirm `main` is checked out → read `current_state.md` →
  pick a token that is not on cooldown → call `claude --print` → on a rate-limit
  banner, put that account on cooldown and retry the same iteration on the next
  token → rebase on `origin/main` and push → stop on `done`, on `blocked`, or at
  the iteration cap.

## Safety model

Every commit lands on `main` and is pushed immediately — a deliberate choice
made in July 2026, not an oversight. There is no branch or worktree cushion, so
if the target repository auto-deploys on push, each iteration reaches production
with no human review in between. The guardrails that replaced the cushion are
not configurable: `git push --force` and `git reset --hard` are blocked through
`--disallowedTools`; the run refuses to start on any branch but `main`;
`--max-iterations` is required with no unlimited default; and `status: blocked`
is a first-class ending that stops the loop for a human instead of forcing
progress. Review the scope in `macro_plan.md` before a run, not the diff after.

## Running it

Requires Node 18 or newer and a Claude Code CLI login. Set
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` for a single account, or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKENS`
with a comma-separated pool — the pool is the reason the cooldown logic exists,
since a run can keep going on the next account instead of sleeping five hours.

    node src/runner.mjs "/path/to/target-repo" --max-iterations 20
    npm run ui   # optional local UI on http://127.0.0.1:4517, loopback only
